thread:
maria: quick heads-up — hitting intermittent slow-consumer behaviour in the Python SSE client after an auth refresh. partial JSON objects arriving in tiny chunks, and our reader pauses to refresh token which seems to let the inbound buffer spike. anyone seen this?

maria: repro notes: aiohttp client, using `async for chunk in resp.content.iter_any()`; when we pause the consumer to refresh the token we sometimes get dozens of 1-5 byte fragments that make the incremental json parser choke. sometimes leads to backlog and then consumer falls behind (app-level backpressure).

maria: minimal snippet:```py
async for chunk in resp.content.iter_chunked(1024):
    buf += chunk
    try:
        obj, used = incremental_parse(buf)
        buf = buf[used:]
        handle(obj)
    except Incomplete:
        # pause work here while we refresh token
        await refresh_token()
```

aj: pinging @maria — can you paste logs around the refresh? is the client actually awaiting on a lock when refresh happens?

maria: logs show around refresh we return early from the parser loop and then `await refresh_token()` blocks ~400-800ms sometimes. chunks keep coming and buffer grows.

tara: we saw similar with the JS client — fix was to keep consuming the socket while refresh happens, move parsing to a background task + a bounded queue. dropping or stashing partial frames helped. avoids pausing the TCP window.

kevin: yeah background reader + queue is the pattern. small bounded queue -> when full, either apply backpressure by yielding control to the receive loop (so server's TCP window slows) or drop oldest partials if liveness > completeness.

kevin: example sketch:```py
# reader
async def reader(resp, q):
    async for chunk in resp.content.iter_any():
        await q.put(chunk)  # bounded -> blocks producer if full

# parser
async def parser(q):
    buf = b''
    while True:
        chunk = await q.get()
        buf += chunk
        try:
            obj, used = incremental_parse(buf)
            buf = buf[used:]
            handle(obj)
        except Incomplete:
            continue
```

sam: FWIW we added a default 8KB bounded queue in the Java client and it fixed the cascade. also add a lightweight keepalive/heartbeat event so server knows client alive during refresh.

maria: thanks. I pushed a PR that changes py client to background reader + asyncio.Queue(maxsize=8192) + small keepalive ping while refreshing. PR: #4521. Asking for review @aj @kevin.

aj: looking now. quick thought — rather than blocking on `await q.put()` when full, consider `try_put_nowait()` + backoff to allow adaptive drop policy. we had one case where blocking the reader starved the event loop during GC.

kevin: agree. also add metrics: queue_length, fragments_per_msg, parse_fail_rate so we can detect regressions.

maria: added metrics and instrumented the keepalive. also added unit tests for fragmented JSON (repro case).

sam: CI flaked on the fragile timing tests — I added a hermetic test variant that injects chunk delays instead of sleeping. mark the timing-based test as flaky on slow runners.

ci-bot: CI passed for PR #4521 (linux, py3.11) — integration tests for streaming enabled.

aj: quick review done, left two minor comments about exceptions and log levels. lgtm after those.

maria: thanks all — will address comments and merge. follow-up: open an ops ticket to add queue_length alert to streaming dashboards.

tara: nice. saving notes for the JS side too — we'll align patterns across SDKs. :thumbsup:
